principle: The ZHI world scene catalog is open-ended. New scenes may be created as needed; the catalog is not limited to the initial scene list.
creation_rules: Mia may add a new scene JSON file and register it in world-manifest.json when she has a concrete reason or receives a scene request.
Every new scene must receive a stable, unique scene_id and a unique file path.
New scenes must include provenance, verification_status, coordinate references, and links to geometry, entities, navigation, and interactions data.
Unknown coordinates, dimensions, entrances, and connections must remain null or explicitly unverified; do not fill gaps with guessed values.
A scene may be a sub-scene, room, building, outdoor area, hidden space, or future concept. Its parent relationship must be explicit when known.
Creating a scene file does not mean the scene is live, rendered, connected to the ZHI runtime, or physically reachable by an agent.
Before runtime integration, validate schema, stable IDs, coordinate mapping, navigation links, interaction permissions, and duplicate scene IDs.
Scene files describe spatial content only. Agent identity, relationships, memories, emotions, movement execution, and arrival status remain controlled by their existing authoritative ZHI systems.
Mia can create files on an authorized development branch or propose a patch; changes to the main branch require the repository's normal review/approval workflow.
scene_id_policy: lowercase-kebab-case; stable after publication; never reuse a retired ID
catalog_update_policy: Register each new scene in world-manifest.json; do not replace existing entries or assume the list is exhaustive.
